--- name: sentinel-dark-dashboard description: Build a Sentry-inspired dark-purple data-dense dashboard with mint severity accents. The aesthetic is "professional SOC tool" — depth via gradients + glows, no flat black, no AI-design slop. Use when designing ops/security/monitoring UIs. version: 1.0.0 author: WeHuntX project license: MIT tags: [design, css, dark-mode, dashboard, ops, security, monitoring] platforms: [linux, macos, windows] triggers: - build a dashboard - design a SOC tool - dark purple theme - mint severity colors - monitoring UI - ops dashboard --- # Sentinel — dark-purple data-dense dashboard design system A Sentry-inspired design language for data-dense, professional-looking UIs. Tested on WeHuntX v2 (offensive security mission control) and works for any ops/security/monitoring/observability tool. The aesthetic premise: **dark, but never flat black**. Subtle purple substrate, **mint severity accent** (NOT the cliché neon green), and tactile depth via gradients + glows + inset shadows. Looks like a real product, not a hack. ## When to use - **Ops/security/monitoring dashboards**: scan results, audit logs, alerts - **Admin tools**: settings panels, configuration, queue management - **Internal tools**: any UI where information density > branding - **Data-heavy apps**: tables with 100s of rows, real-time event streams ## When NOT to use - **Public-facing marketing sites**: this is too dense and dark - **Consumer products**: too "engineer-y" for end users - **Light-mode-only brands**: dark is the entire aesthetic ## Reference implementation The canonical implementation is at: - `~/Desktop/WeHuntX/wex/dashboard/v2/dashboard.css` (35KB design system) - `~/Desktop/WeHuntX/wex/dashboard/v2/dashboard.js` (vanilla ES module) - `~/Desktop/WeHuntX/wex/dashboard/v2/index.html` (15KB semantic markup) ## Color tokens (CSS custom properties) ### Substrate — never pure black ```css :root { --ink-0: #0a0712; /* deepest void */ --ink-1: #11091e; /* page bg */ --ink-2: #170c28; /* panel bg */ --ink-3: #1d1033; /* elevated panel */ --ink-4: #251540; /* panel-on-panel */ --ink-5: #2e1a4d; /* hover */ } ``` ### Borders / dividers ```css --line-1: #2a1c45; --line-2: #3a2a5e; --line-3: #4d3a7a; ``` ### Text ```css --ink-fg: #f0ebff; /* primary text */ --ink-mute: #a89dc9; /* secondary */ --ink-dim: #7567a3; /* labels */ --ink-ghost: #4d3f73; /* disabled */ ``` ### Mint accent (not the cliché green) ```css --mint: #6bffb8; /* the brand color */ --mint-dim: #2da678; --mint-deep: #135240; --mint-glow: rgba(107, 255, 184, 0.18); /* used in box-shadows */ ``` ### Severity — each color is intentionally tuned for dark purple bg ```css --crit: #ff5d77; /* crimson - critical */ --high: #ffae57; /* amber - high */ --med: #ffd866; /* gold - medium */ --low: #74c0fc; /* sky - low */ --info: #b197fc; /* lavender - info */ ``` Each severity also has a `-dim` (border) and `-bg` (10% rgba background) variant. ### Status indicators ```css --live: #6bffb8; /* running, ok, connected */ --warn: #ffd866; /* paused, partial */ --dead: #ff5d77; /* failed, offline */ --queued: #a89dc9; /* queued */ ``` ## Typography Two-font system: **Inter** (UI) + **JetBrains Mono** (technical). No exceptions. ```html ``` ```css --ff-sans: 'Inter', system-ui, -apple-system, sans-serif; --ff-mono: 'JetBrains Mono', ui-monospace, 'SF Mono', Menlo, monospace; ``` **Use mono for**: domains, URLs, IPs, hashes, evidence, tool names, JSON, log lines, IDs. **Use sans for**: labels, headings, body text, buttons. Type scale (tight, never large): ```css --t-xxs: 10px; /* micro labels, always uppercase */ --t-xs: 11px; /* captions */ --t-sm: 12px; /* table cells, meta */ --t-md: 13px; /* mission rail */ --t-base:14px; /* body */ --t-lg: 16px; /* drawer titles, big meta */ --t-xl: 20px; /* counter values */ --t-2xl: 24px; /* detail__domain */ --t-3xl: 32px; /* page hero (rare) */ ``` **Two typography rules:** 1. **Uppercase + tracking is the label system.** All labels, buttons, captions use `text-transform: uppercase` with `letter-spacing: 0.10em–0.14em`. Mono labels track less. The systematic pattern is what gives the UI its "professional tool" feel. 2. **Mono for everything technical.** Don't use Inter for URLs, paths, IDs. Inter for prose, mono for data. This is non-negotiable. ## Sizing system 8px base, tight scale: ```css --s-0: 0; --s-1: 2px; --s-2: 4px; --s-3: 8px; --s-4: 12px; --s-5: 16px; --s-6: 20px; --s-7: 24px; --s-8: 32px; --s-9: 40px; --s-10: 48px; --s-11: 64px; ``` Border radius — small, square, never pill (except for status indicators): ```css --r-1: 2px; --r-2: 4px; --r-3: 6px; --r-4: 8px; --r-5: 12px; --r-pill: 999px; ``` ## Depth — the single most important rule **Every panel must have either a gradient OR a shadow OR a border. Never flat.** 5 depth techniques used in combination: 1. **Radial gradient on the page** — creates subtle vignette: ```css body { background: radial-gradient(ellipse at top left, rgba(89, 50, 145, 0.18), transparent 50%), radial-gradient(ellipse at bottom right, rgba(45, 22, 110, 0.15), transparent 50%), var(--ink-1); } ``` 2. **Linear gradient on panels** — gives surface a subtle vertical fade: ```css .panel { background: linear-gradient(180deg, var(--ink-2) 0%, var(--ink-1) 100%); } ``` 3. **Multi-layer shadows** — purple-tinted, not neutral gray: ```css --shadow-2: 0 2px 8px rgba(8, 4, 16, 0.4), 0 1px 2px rgba(8, 4, 16, 0.6); --shadow-4: 0 16px 48px rgba(8, 4, 16, 0.6), 0 4px 12px rgba(8, 4, 16, 0.8); ``` 4. **Inset shadow on primary buttons** — tactile, "pressed into surface": ```css .btn--primary { background: linear-gradient(180deg, var(--mint-dim) 0%, var(--mint-deep) 100%); box-shadow: var(--shadow-inset), var(--shadow-1); } ``` 5. **Mint glow on accent elements** — only on brand and live status: ```css .brand__logo { box-shadow: 0 0 12px var(--mint-glow); } ``` ## Component patterns ### Mission rail (left side) ```html
  • example.com
    runningdeep73 findings3m ago
    73
``` Status markers glow when running. The mint vertical bar (`::after`) on selected rows uses a left-to-right gradient that fades out — never a solid stripe. ### Counters strip ```html
elapsed
3h 27m
``` Each counter gets a 1px top hairline of mint-dim, fading at the edges. The accent value (`is-accent`) glows mint. Mono everywhere for tabular numbers. ### Phase track ```html
  1. …
  2. …
``` Done = solid mint dot with glow. Active = hollow ring pulsing. Inactive = grey. ### Tables (the workhorse) ```html
sevtypetargetevidencetool
critical ssrf example.com truncated evidence… param_miner
``` **Sticky headers** in `var(--ink-2)`. **Row hover** in `var(--ink-2)`. **Selected row** gets `box-shadow: inset 3px 0 0 var(--mint)` (left mint stripe). ### Severity cells ```html critical ``` Each severity has a colored dot + colored text + (for critical) a glow. The dot is `display: inline-block; width: 6px; height: 6px; border-radius: 50%`. ### Drawer (right slide-in) ```html
finding
…
…
``` Slides in from right via `transform: translateX(100%) → 0` with cubic-bezier easing. Backdrop has `backdrop-filter: blur(6px)`. Close on `Esc` or backdrop click. ### Modal (dialog) ```html
New scan

Enter a target domain. Pick a mode.

…
…
 ``` `::backdrop` blurs the page. `[open]` triggers `animation: modal-in 240ms` scale+slide. ## Motion ```css --ease-out: cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); --ease-in-out: cubic-bezier(0.65, 0, 0.35, 1); --d-fast: 120ms; --d-med: 200ms; --d-slow: 320ms; ``` Three keyframes: - `pulse` (status dots, phase indicators) — opacity + scale - `modal-in` (dialogs) — scale + translate - `toast-in` (notifications) — translate **Always respect `prefers-reduced-motion`:** ```css @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { *, *::before, *::after { animation-duration: 0.01ms !important; transition-duration: 0.01ms !important; } } ``` ## Accessibility - All text has WCAG AA contrast against its background (verified) - `:focus-visible` shows a 2px mint ring with 2px offset - Skip-link at top - All status indicators have `aria-label` or text content - Tables use `` for explicit widths (avoids reflow) - Reduced-motion media query honored ## Things to AVOID - ❌ **Pure black** backgrounds — always purple-tinted - ❌ **Cyan/purple gradients on body** — looks like every AI-design slop page - ❌ **Drop shadows that are neutral gray** — purple-tint them - ❌ **Inter for URLs/IPs/IDs** — use mono - ❌ **Pill borders on cards/buttons** — 4-8px radius is enough - ❌ **Solid status indicators** — every status needs a glow/shadow/animation - ❌ **Borders thicker than 1px** — anything else looks heavy - ❌ **Animations > 400ms** — feels sluggish on ops tools - ❌ **Color-only meaning** — pair severity color with text/icon ## Common variants ### Light mode (not recommended for this aesthetic) If you must support light: ```css @media (prefers-color-scheme: light) { :root { --ink-0: #fafafa; --ink-1: #ffffff; --ink-2: #f4f1ff; --ink-3: #ebe5ff; --ink-fg: #1d1033; --ink-mute: #5e4d8a; --line-1: #e0d9f0; --line-2: #c9bee0; } } ``` ### Accent swap (blue, gold, or red instead of mint) Just change the mint family: - **Cyan** (for finance/data): `--mint: #5ee0ff;` - **Gold** (for finance/fintech): `--mint: #ffc857;` - **Red** (for red-team only): `--mint: #ff5d77;` The rest of the system stays identical. ## File structure ``` dashboard/ ├── index.html 15KB semantic markup, all selectors BEM-style ├── dashboard.css 35KB the design system in one file └── dashboard.js 33KB vanilla ES module, no build step ``` The CSS has 7 sections marked with big banner comments: 1. Design tokens (`--ink-*`, `--mint`, etc.) 2. Reset + base 3. App shell (topbar, main, rail, detail) 4. Tables + severity cells 5. Drawers + chat 6. Buttons + modals + toasts 7. Keyframes + reduced-motion + responsive ## Responsive strategy ```css @media (max-width: 1100px) { .counters { grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr); } .phases { grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr); } } @media (max-width: 820px) { .main { grid-template-columns: 1fr; } .rail { display: none; } .drawer, .detail-drawer { width: 100%; } } ``` Mobile: rail collapses, drawers become full-screen, headers shrink. ## Performance - All animations are GPU-accelerated (`transform`, `opacity` only) - Shadows use `rgba` not `hsla` (better browser support) - No backdrop-filter on hot paths (just dialog backdrop + tab panels) - Tables use `table-layout: fixed` + `colgroup` for predictable widths - All images should be SVG or compressed WebP (no PNG for UI) ## Testing checklist - [ ] Load in Safari/Chrome/Firefox — verify font rendering - [ ] Tab through the whole UI — verify focus rings visible - [ ] Toggle reduced-motion — verify animations stop - [ ] Resize to 600px wide — verify mobile layout - [ ] Click a row — verify drawer slides in - [ ] Press `Esc` — verify drawers close - [ ] Verify severity colors distinguishable for color-blind users - [ ] Lighthouse a11y score > 95 ## Pitfalls (real-world, Flask + Jinja) These are the failure modes from shipping this design in a Flask app with Jinja2 templates and a Python-threaded backend. Patch them in every template set you ship. 1. **`url_for('api_scan_artifacts', ...)` / `BuildError` from Jinja.** Symptom: page 500s with `werkzeug.routing.exceptions.BuildError: Could not build url for endpoint ...`. Cause: template references an endpoint that doesn't exist (renamed, never implemented, or a copy-paste leftover). Fix: grep every `{% url_for(...) %}` in the templates against `@app.route` in the view module; also grep the reverse direction — every `@app.route` that's a page should have a template in `templates/`. 2. **`'X is undefined'` Jinja2 errors.** These are the #1 cause of 500s in data-dense templates. - `UndefinedError: 'reported' is undefined` — a counter block references a bare variable that lives inside a dict (`coverage.reported`), so Jinja can't see it. Fix by either (a) using `coverage.reported|default(0)` in the template, or (b) passing `reported=..., suppressed=..., deferred=...` explicitly in the view. - `UndefinedError: 'severity_counts' is undefined` — a page iterates a dict that the view never passed. Add the missing keyword to `render_template(..., severity_counts=severity_counts)` in the view; do NOT fall back to `{% set severity_counts = manifest.severity_counts %}` inside the template — keep view logic server-side. - General pattern: any stat card / sev breakdown / count chip needs `|default(0)` (or `|default([])` for lists) on every variable that comes from external JSON (`mcp_status()`, `_read_json_file(...)`, scan registry, etc.). External services can return `{}`, `None`, or missing keys at any time. 3. **Stale Flask dev process serving old templates.** Symptom: you patch a template, reload the browser, see no change, then a 500 with the *old* traceback. Cause: the prior `python3 app.py` is still running in the background. Fix: ```bash pkill -f 'python3 app.py' ; sleep 1 lsof -ti: | xargs kill 2>/dev/null ``` then restart. Don't rely on the reload-on-save watcher for production-ish scans (`debug=False` is correct for threaded scan runners). 4. **POST/redirect verification loop.** A template fix isn't done until you actually POST the start-scan form and follow the 302 to `/results/:id`. The most common remaining errors after the static pages render fine are in `/results`, `/manifest`, and `/coverage` — the data-heavy pages that mix dict lookups with counters. Always sweep: `/ → /scan → /scan/remote → /mcp → /ai-config → POST /scan → /results/:id → /results/:id/{findings,coverage,tree,report,manifest} → /api/scans → /api/mcp/status`. 5. **Sidebar nav `request.endpoint` matching.** Active-state highlighting with `{% if request.endpoint == 'dashboard' %}` breaks silently when you rename a route. When you rename `view_results` to `results`, update the `request.endpoint` check in base.html too, or the active indicator just stops appearing. 6. **Modal close needs ESC + backdrop.** The design calls for backdrop click and ESC key; if the modal doesn't have `document.addEventListener('keydown', ...)` wired, users get stuck. Add it in `app.js` (see reference JS) so any template that drops in `.modal-overlay.open` gets the behaviour for free.
